text:
Sam: Quick RFC follow-up — I'm proposing we canonicalize a small set of observability attribute keys at the edge (proxy/sidecar) so downstream pipelines and cost attribution don't rely on fragile client keys. Short version: one canonical header + a stable fallback mapping table.
Maria: +1. Can you sketch the keys? We need to know impact on sampling and billing lookup.
Sam: Draft mapping below (edge normalizes incoming headers -> outgoing X-Obs-*):

```
Incoming: tenant_id | tenant | x-tenant -> X-Obs-Tenant
Incoming: svc_env | env -> X-Obs-Env
Incoming: billing_key | account_id -> X-Obs-Billing
Incoming: trace_id | x-trace-id -> X-Obs-Trace
```

Sam: We only canonicalize, not drop originals — inject X-Obs-* and add a small provenance flag `X-Obs-Orig-Keys` with comma list. That gives pipelines time to migrate.
Josh: Love the provenance flag. A couple of notes:
- Proxy CPU impact: adding header ops per request is <1% on our dataplane in perf tests but needs canary.
- KV cache: if billing_key gets remapped, cost-aggregation must use X-Obs-Billing or we'll double-count.
Anya: For the sampling interaction: if we remap tenant -> X-Obs-Tenant earlier we can do sampling decisions consistently in edge. But we should surface the original sampling hint if present. Maybe `X-Obs-SampleHint`.
Kevin: What about multi-tenant requests where both `tenant_id` and `account_id` are present and disagree? Do we prefer one source? We should pick deterministic order: client header > auth token > query param.
Sam: Agreed on precedence. I'll add that to the doc. Proposed order: client header > auth token claims > query param > default none.
Maria: Migration plan thoughts:
1) Phase A (2 weeks): edge starts injecting X-Obs-* but pipelines keep reading originals. Add metrics to track % of traffic with X-Obs-Billing present.
2) Phase B (4 weeks): switch consumer pipelines to prefer X-Obs-* but still accept originals. Add regression alerts for cost deltas.
3) Phase C: Deprecate originals after 30d of stable reads.

Maria: Also we need a backfill story for historical traces/metrics for the cost reconciliation job.
Sam: For backfill: we can run a transform job that reads stored events, infers canonical keys using same precedence, and writes a canonicalized envelope to the billing table. This is heavy but one-off.
Josh: Implementation detail: edge sidecar will expose a feature flag `obs.canonicalize=true` and a rollout percent. We should also add an opt-out tag for customers that need raw headers.
Anya: Query compatibility: analytics dashboards will need an alias layer so saved queries keep working while we flip to X-Obs-*. We'll document alias -> X-Obs-*.
Kevin: Edge case: internal service-to-service calls that don't include tenant info. If auth token has no tenant, we must not invent one — prefer empty and let billing fallback to routing. Otherwise we misattribute cost.
Sam: Good call. Will add guard: only propagate X-Obs-Billing if we can validate against auth claims pattern (regex) or a token introspect.
ingest-bot: Deploy-check: canary pool size required = 1% of ingress. Add job to perf-runbook: `obs-edge-header-canary`.
Maria: Owners? Sam on the RFC and edge changes, Josh for runtime perf + canary infra, Anya for sampling interaction and queries, Kevin for billing reconciliation/backfill.
Sam: I'll open a short RFC doc and a rollout checklist. Tagging @here for visibility. Anyone object to this path? :eyes:
Kevin: No objections. Thanks — will prep the backfill plan.
Josh: SGTM. I'll schedule perf run tomorrow.
Anya: SGTM from analytics side. We'll add dashboard aliases.
Maria: Ok let's go ahead with Phase A next week. :rocket:
